summary: Documented PARAMETER defaults on the Modelfile reference: num_ctx 2048, temperature 0.8, seed 0, top_k 40, top_p 0.9, min_p 0.0, repeat_last_n 64 (0 disabled, -1 = num_ctx), num_predict -1 (infinite). stop has no default and is repeated once per pattern. (from docs.ollama.com)

Only FROM is required in a Modelfile; PARAMETER, TEMPLATE, SYSTEM, ADAPTER, LICENSE, MESSAGE and REQUIRES are optional. Instructions are case-insensitive and may appear in any order.

Hermes specifically is a textbook case of the /v1 problem. Hermes computes a context window for each request and sends num_ctx, but it talks to a local Ollama over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so Ollama ignores it and every model loads at the server default. A native /api/chat adapter is in progress upstream (hermes-agent PR #4505), and there's a community stopgap package that reroutes Hermes to the native endpoint until it lands. Until then, OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH is the fix for Hermes users, full stop.
Starting from an existing model's definition is the recommended authoring path: `ollama show --modelfile <model>` prints its Modelfile including TEMPLATE and parameters.
The original pretrained weights are kept frozen, which means you can have multiple lightweight and portable LoRA models for various downstream tasks built on top of them.

The current docs.ollama.com import page covers only whole-model Safetensors and GGUF import and shows no adapter workflow. The current Modelfile reference source (docs/modelfile.mdx on main) contains no occurrence of 'adapter' or 'lora'. The only documented ADAPTER guidance found is in the older 0.9.0 guide.

Template syntax is model-specific: copying another model's TEMPLATE breaks output, and after replacing TEMPLATE the stop parameters must be reset to that model's special tokens. SYSTEM only takes effect if the TEMPLATE contains a .System block.

TEMPLATE uses Go text/template syntax; documented variables are {{ .System }}, {{ .Prompt }} and {{ .Response }}, and text after {{ .Response }} is omitted when generating. The reference page does not document .Messages, .Tools or .Think.

Merging a PEFT LoRA into a quantized base re-quantizes the base weight, so repeated merge/unmerge cycles accumulate rounding error; for deployment prefer one merge_and_unload() (assign the returned model) and keep the unmerged adapter, which supports merging offline before an Ollama FROM import as an alternative to ADAPTER.

ADAPTER points at a LoRA adapter (GGUF or safetensors) and requires FROM to name the base model the adapter was tuned on; a mismatched base gives unstable behavior. The official Modelfile reference page fetched here has no ADAPTER section, and the import page does not cover it.

FROM accepts an existing library model (name:tag), a safetensors model directory, or a GGUF file path (absolute or relative to the Modelfile). Split GGUF is supported with a wildcard (FROM ./model-*.gguf) or one FROM line per shard.

For a GGUF adapter, write FROM <model name> and ADAPTER /path/to/file.gguf. FROM may be an Ollama model, a GGUF file or a Safetensors model. A GGUF adapter comes from llama.cpp's convert_lora_to_gguf.py or a download such as Hugging Face.

* converting a Safetensors model with the `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` from Llama.cpp; * converting a Safetensors adapter with the `convert_lora_to_gguf.py` from Llama.cpp; or * downloading a model or adapter from a place such as HuggingFace

REQUIRES <version> sets the minimum Ollama version (example 0.14.0), and a CAPABILITY instruction adds capabilities to GGUF/MLX models; the reference page also lists a draft_num_predict parameter (4 for separate draft models, 0 disables speculative drafting). These are recent additions.

The Modelfile reference documents num_ctx default 2048, while the Ollama FAQ says the default context window is 4096 tokens. OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH overrides the server default; per-request num_ctx goes in the API options object, and PARAMETER num_ctx bakes it into a model.
SYSTEM and LICENSE take triple-quoted text (SYSTEM """..."""). LICENSE records license text in the model; the build/run commands are `ollama create <name> -f ./Modelfile` then `ollama run <name>`.

Per the 0.9.0 import guide, Safetensors adapters are supported for Llama (2, 3, 3.1, 3.2), Mistral (1, 2, Mixtral) and Gemma (1, 2) architectures. Adapters can be produced by Hugging Face training, Unsloth or MLX.

Make sure that you use the same base model in the `FROM` command as you used to create the adapter otherwise you will get erratic results. Most frameworks use different quantization methods, so it's best to use non-quantized (i.e. non-QLoRA) adapters. If your adapter is in the same directory as your `Modelfile`, use `ADAPTER .` to specify the adapter path.

llama.cpp ships an export-lora tool that applies one or more LoRA adapters (--lora, comma-separated, or --lora-scaled FNAME:SCALE) to a base model and writes a merged GGUF, f16 by default. This is an alternative to ADAPTER: merge offline, then import the merged file with plain FROM.
